title: Creative Guy
transcript: It doesn't always take a genius to win a losing position. Sometimes it's enough to be a little bit creative in this position. It seems like despite black having an extra rook and two pawns, there is simply going to be a textbook checkmate with the rook and queen. But if we try to do this, we soon realize that there is an issue. The queen is actually pinned to the king all the way on the other side of the board. But luckily, white can keep giving checks with this rook. And now at the very least we can secure a draw by keep giving checks like this. But what's the glory in taking a draw? In this position, white has successfully unpinned the queen because now there is a rook in the way. And so after the king moves, he can play queen to c7 check and push the king to the edge. And now again after this check, there is an opportunity to simply repeat moves and get a draw. But there's a very creative little method to actually win this game for white. Can you see it? After the king moves, we start shuffling the king down towards the king. And it doesn't matter what the black king does because eventually the queen reaches B2. And now it stands between the king and the rook, meaning that the rook is not pinned anymore. And after the king moves, we're going to be able to deliver this simple but nonetheless beautiful checkmate.
